_comment: What the drift watch expects to be true. A repository is listed here because
somebody decided its shape deliberately — not because it happened to be set
that way. Adding a repository is a decision; the file is the record of it.
`actions` and `.github` are public ON PURPOSE: `.github` serves org defaults,
and `actions` holds reusable workflows other orgs' repos call. Everything else
is private. So this cannot be a blanket 'must be private' rule.
`runner_groups` is the same idea for self-hosted runners. A runner group is
the only thing standing between a fork's pull request on a public repository
and code running on our own hardware, on the office LAN. It is one toggle,
it lives in a settings page nobody visits, and flipping it leaves no trace.
So: `allows_public_repositories` false, and `datum-private` scoped to the
repositories listed here and no others. A group that appears is drift too.
